messages.subject: qplot density plot color by
parts:
I have some data (below) that has multiple biological samples and for
each sample multiple measurement replicates.

sampleID replicateID value
sample1 sample1_rep1 249
sample1 sample1_rep1 440
sample1 sample1_rep2 375
sample1 sample1_rep2 222
sample1 sample1_rep1 451
sample1 sample1_rep2 387
sample2 sample2_rep1 21
sample2 sample2_rep1 16
sample2 sample2_rep1 20
sample2 sample2_rep2 14
sample2 sample2_rep2 19
sample2 sample2_rep2 9

I generate a density plot of the values split into different
measurement replicates using the qplot command below.

library(ggplot2)
df <- data.frame(value,ReplicateID)
qplot(value, data = df, geom="density", color=replicateID)
ggsave("Plot.png", width = 16, height = 10, dpi=72)

I'm wondering if it is possible to split the density plot by
replicateID, but color by SampleID so the replicates of the same
sample will have the same color?

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: qplot density plot color by
parts:
Hi Doug,

Does this do what you want?

qplot(value, data = df, geom = "density",
group = replicateID, colour = sampleID)

As you want more and more customized graphs, I often find it easier to
work with the individual layers rather than qplot(). Here is the same
thing a different way:

ggplot(df, aes(x = value, group = replicateID, colour = sampleID)) +
geom_density()

Hope this helps,

Josh
